title: Nonlocal Kondo-exchange-driven intrinsic anomalous Hall effect in localized-$4f$ antiferromagnetic metals
abstract: The anomalous Hall effect in antiferromagnetic metals has attracted considerable attention. Most known realizations involve itinerant $d$ electrons that simultaneously mediate charge transport and magnetic order. Here, we focus on $f$-electron materials, where localized magnetic moments and conduction electrons are hosted in different orbitals. We develop a theoretical framework to describe the impact of localized antiferromagnetic order on itinerant electrons. Applying this approach to the recently discovered $4f$ antiferromagnetic metal $\mathrm{Ce}_{2}\mathrm{Cu}\mathrm{Ge}_{6}$, we identify the origin of both the intrinsic anomalous Hall conductivity and the spin splitting of the energy bands as spin-dependent intersite hopping induced by nonlocal Kondo exchange coupling, rather than a Zeeman-type effective field acting locally on the conduction electrons.
summary: The paper theoretically investigates the anomalous Hall effect in $f$-electron antiferromagnets by developing an effective Hamiltonian derived from strong correlation physics. It concludes that the AHE is fundamentally driven by nonlocal spin-dependent hopping mediated by Kondo exchange coupling, rather than local magnetic fields or itinerant electron behavior alone.
main_problem: The study aims to elucidate the microscopic origin of the intrinsic anomalous Hall effect (AHE) in antiferromagnetic $f$-electron metals, particularly where localized magnetic moments interact with itinerant conduction electrons.
main_result: The AHE is found to originate from nonlocal spin-dependent intersite hopping induced by Kondo exchange coupling, rather than a simple local Zeeman field or canting magnetization effect. The $	ext{Ge } 4p$ orbitals provide the dominant contribution to this effect.
method: The authors developed a theoretical framework using Green's function techniques and derived an effective Hamiltonian analogous to the Kondo lattice model, incorporating strong correlation effects via approximations like Hubbard-I.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as a localized-$4f$ antiferromagnetic metal ($	ext{Ce}_2	ext{CuGe}_6$), described by a tight-binding Hamiltonian coupling conduction ($c$) and $f$ electrons. The strong correlations are treated using DMFT/Hubbard-I approximations.
key_observables: Intrinsic Anomalous Hall Conductivity ($\sigma_{DC}^{xy}$), spin splitting of energy bands, and the dependence of $\sigma_{DC}^{xy}$ on canting magnetization ($m_z$).
important_parameters: Kondo temperature ($T_K \simeq 1 	ext{ K}$); hybridization terms ($\hat{V}(\mathbf{k})$); molecular field strengths controlling AFM order.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on deriving an effective Hamiltonian that captures the physics of $c-f$ hybridization, often simplifying by neglecting orbital degeneracy or assuming specific magnetic ordering patterns.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison between local vs. nonlocal contributions to AHE (Figure 1), plot $\sigma_{DC}^{xy}$ dependence on canting magnetization ($m_z$) showing robustness against $m_z$ changes (Figure 2), and show band structure polarization related to spin splitting (Figure 3).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the theoretical necessity of an effective Hamiltonian for correlated systems, deriving this model from a full Green's function approach incorporating strong correlations, and finally applying it to calculate $\sigma_{DC}^{xy}$ while decomposing contributions to pinpoint the nonlocal hopping mechanism.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed many-body theoretical framework connecting magnetic order (AFM) to transport phenomena (AHE) in strongly correlated materials using concepts like Kondo exchange, which are central to understanding complex electronic states beyond simple band theory.
